dedupe_keys.name: observed effects of the may 2024 gannon storm on the new zealand gas pipeline network

description: This study by Malcolm Ingham, Tim Divett, Craig Rodger and Mark Sigley of Victoria University of Wellington and the University of Otago, published in Space Weather in 2025, presents cathodic protection monitoring data from the New Zealand gas pipeline network during the Gannon geomagnetic storm of May 2024. Coverage: potentials between the pipe and a Cu/CuSO4 reference cell and between an installed metal coupon and the reference cell; at some locations both swung widely and became positive for significant lengths of time, taking the pipeline outside the desired protection range, which can lead to corrosion where the coating has defects; highly negative potentials that can detach coating were also observed. The relation between pipe and coupon-off potentials is linear over a wide range but reaches a limit or scatters at some sites, and anode bed to pipe potentials can stand in where pipe potentials are not monitored. Format and access: an open journal article. Licence and cost: free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: one storm; the abstract was the part read. The observed responses can validate simulation of space weather hazard exposure and resilience for pipelines. It relates to the New Zealand pipe-to-soil potential model by the same group and the Argentine cathodic protection study in the catalogue.
